identity.name: Sodium sulfates (sodium sulfate; sodium hydrogen sulfate)
identity.chemical_class: Inorganic sulfate salts (sodium salts of sulfuric acid)

function.mechanism: Dissociates into sodium/sulfate (and hydrogen for E514(ii)) ions, contributing to pH control and ionic-strength effects.
common_food_categories: Meat products (modeled contribution in conservative EFSA scenarios)
Indirect food-contact packaging materials (US CFR context)

adi.basis: EFSA FAF (2019) concluded no need for a numerical ADI for sulfuric acid and sodium/potassium/calcium/ammonium sulfates at reported uses and use levels.

efsa.key_finding: Exposure at reported uses does not raise a safety concern; no concern for genotoxicity/carcinogenicity; refined exposure estimates are below human laxative-effect dose levels.

fda.notes: Affirmed as GRAS for indirect food use (packaging-contact contexts) at levels not exceeding GMP under 21 CFR 186.1(b)(1); direct-addition status for E514 in foods is not established by this section.

adi.basis: JECFA entries for INS 514(i) and 514(ii) report ADI NOT SPECIFIED.

concerns.summary: High oral sulfate doses are associated with osmotic GI effects (loose stools/laxative effects), with human laxative effect around 300 mg sodium sulfate/kg bw noted by EFSA.

A 2025 retrospective single-center study reported higher erosive gastritis/ulcer findings with oral sulfate tablet bowel prep versus PEG, but this reflects high-dose bowel-prep context and is not definitive for food-additive intake levels.
EFSA recommended tightening arsenic/lead/mercury specification limits for sulfate additives to reduce impurity-driven exposure.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA found no concern for genotoxicity and carcinogenicity for the sulfate additive group at reported uses.
EFSA concluded no safety concern at reported use levels and no need for a numerical ADI.
Recent oral sulfate bowel-prep RCTs reported no severe adverse events and generally acceptable safety/tolerability in studied populations.

populations: Toddlers/children (highest modeled intakes in EFSA scenarios)
Individuals with gastrointestinal sensitivity at high bolus sulfate intakes
adi_exceedance.notes: No numerical ADI exists. In EFSA refined non-brand-loyal scenarios (mean 0.4-35; high 3-68 mg sulfate/kg bw/day), exposure is below the reported laxative-effect threshold. Conservative maximum scenarios can approach/exceed that threshold and are considered overestimates by EFSA.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory consensus (EFSA/JECFA/FDA-indirect GRAS context) indicates low concern at authorized uses, with no numerical ADI needed and no genotoxic/carcinogenic concern. Remaining uncertainties are mainly high-dose GI effects, impurity controls, and gaps in modern reproductive/developmental datasets.
key_factors: EFSA 2019: no safety concern at reported uses; no numerical ADI needed
JECFA: ADI NOT SPECIFIED for INS 514(i)/514(ii)
US CFR: GRAS affirmation for indirect food-contact use under GMP (21 CFR 186.1797)
High-dose oral sulfate can cause GI effects; limited clinical signal of gastric mucosal irritation in bowel-prep contexts
No IARC carcinogenic classification identified for sodium sulfate/sodium hydrogen sulfate
